prompts: Remember the little archery games of the Windows 95 days? We want the first level of one, our own, in {WS}/game/index.html, a single file. An archer you aim with the mouse, pulling the bow back for power, balloons to pop, a score on screen, a way to start and a way to lose. How it looks, plays and sounds is your call, and that is what we care about most: a minute of play should be fun, and every shot and hit should feel and sound good. It is reviewed by opening the file, with no build step, in a browser that reaches only Google Fonts, and by playing it.
answers:
[goal] One-file Windows 95-style archery level in ./game/index.html, playable solo.
[action] Built `game/index.html` (canvas + WebAudio, Google Fonts only, no build).
[result] Verified in headless browser: start screen, click START, aim/hold/release fires an arrow with the draw meter, HUD/lives render, no errors. Score stayed 0 on a test shot into empty sky; the loop runs (balloons rise and escape, hearts tick down).
[next] Play it; tweak feel (gravity, spawn rate, win score) if you want harder/easier.

Assumptions and notes:
- Win condition: reach 500 points (clear level). Lose: three hearts gone (balloon escapes; arrows that miss don't cost hearts in this cut).
- Controls: mouse aim, hold to draw (with predicted dotted arc and power bar), release to loosen; touch supported (touchstart/move/end).
- Audio is synthesized: draw ticks, bow twang/whoosh, pop burst, miss/lose/win jingles. No external assets.
- I could not view screenshots (model has no image input), so visuals are code-reviewed, not eye-inspected.

Known trade-offs: a missed arrow currently only shows via physics; misses cost no heart. The balloons-escape-costs-heart loop gives the real loss path.
